messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — I'll open a Terraform PR in a few to tweak the statefulset rollout params for session-store. We're seeing a small spike of restarts when we scale >2 pods at once. Thinking to reduce burstiness by limiting maxSurge and adding a small maxUnavailable so new pods come up more safely.

tara: SGTM in principle. Can you paste the exact k8s snippet? worried about long init containers + PVC bind race. :thinking_face: 

alex: Sure. Plan is to change strategy to RollingUpdate and set:
```yaml
strategy:
  type: RollingUpdate
  rollingUpdate:
    maxSurge: 1
    maxUnavailable: 0
```
Also bump the startupProbe to 90s for this workload. Init takes ~45s with PVC attach + warm cache.

juan: Two quick Qs: (1) Are we relying on ordinal ordering in the STS anywhere? (2) Any impact on autoscaler/hpa when maxUnavailable=0?

alex: (1) No ordinal logic used, just a plain STS with PVC per replica. (2) HPA will still kill/add pods based on metrics, but during a rollout maxUnavailable=0 prevents evicting old pods until new are ready — should be safer. We might see slower capacity reclaim though.

sam: What about PVC binding delays in the cloud? If PV provisioning takes 30-60s we could end up with more Pending pods and block rollout. Maybe we should add a small startupProbe grace or pre-warm volume.

alex: Good call. I'll increase startupProbe.initialDelaySeconds to 10 and failureThreshold to 18 (90s). Also adding a small init job to pre-create directories if needed.

tara: Can you also include a terraform plan note so infra oncall can eyeball it? Last time the provider bumped and changed default reclaimPolicy. 

alex: Yep. PR will include: 
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_stateful_set" "session_store" {
  spec {
    update_strategy {
      type = "RollingUpdate"
      rolling_update {
        max_surge = 1
        max_unavailable = 0
      }
    }
    template { ... }
  }
}
```
And I'll pin the provider to the last working minor.

infra-ci: alex pushed branch alex/sts-rollout-burst-fix — terraform fmt OK. Plan shows changes to statefulset.spec.updateStrategy. No provider upgrades detected.

juan: Would be nice to include a short rollback note in the PR description in case we see readiness regressions. e.g., how to revert to previous strategy quickly.

alex: Will do. Revert steps: apply previous TF statefulset with max_surge=2, max_unavailable=1 and rollback by kubectl rollout undo sts/session-store if needed. I'll also include `kubectl rollout status sts/session-store -w` in the runbook.

sam: One more: do we need a canary? maybe patch 1 replica in staging first.

alex: Plan: staging -> canary in prod (1 replica on prod tag) -> full rollout over 30m. I'll add a flag to the module to control canary weight.

tara: Thanks — ping me when the PR is up. I'll do a quick review and watch the plan. :thumbsup:

alex: PR opened: https://git.redwood/sessions/infra/pulls/42 — includes yaml + terraform + runbook. CC @tara @juan.

infra-ci: CI: terraform plan successful, no diffs to provider. K8s lint passed.

juan: Reviewed the plan, lgtm for staging. Two tiny comments on docs.

sam: Nice. I'll schedule a 10m window tomorrow 09:30 PT to watch prod canary if you want company.

alex: Awesome — thanks all. I'll land after LGTM and runbook ack.
